title: How To Implement Google's Responsive Search Ads - Ten Thousand Foot View

facts.fact: Responsive Search Ads (RSAs) offer up to 3 headlines and 2 description texts, compared with 2 headlines and 1 description text for Expanded Text Ads (ETAs), according to the vendor.
facts.quote: this new ad format offers up to 3 headlines and 2 description texts compared with Expanded Text Ads’ (ETAs) 2 headlines and 1 description text

facts.fact: The vendor states that RSAs provide 90% more text in search ads than ETAs.
facts.quote: That’s 90% more text available in your search ads!

facts.fact: An RSA can contain up to 15 different headlines.
facts.quote: you can create up to 15 different headlines and 4 different descriptions.

facts.fact: An RSA can contain up to 4 different descriptions.
facts.quote: you can create up to 15 different headlines and 4 different descriptions.

facts.fact: Google claims that ad groups with RSAs generate 5-15% more clicks on average (a Google claim, not verified by the vendor).
facts.quote: Google claims that ad groups with RSAs generate between 5-15% more clicks on average.

facts.fact: The RSA editor presents 5 headlines and 2 description texts by default, instead of the 2 headlines and 1 description used in ETAs.
facts.quote: Instead of 2 headlines and 1 description text you’ll be presented with 5 headlines and 2 description texts.

facts.fact: Google recommends creating at least 5 headlines for an RSA.
facts.quote: Google recommends creating at least 5 headlines, which makes sense

facts.fact: The vendor advises against creating more than 1 RSA per ad group.
facts.quote: Don’t create more than 1 RSA per ad group!

facts.fact: Google recommends against using RSAs in branded ad groups.
facts.quote: Google recommends against using RSAs in branded ad groups.

facts.fact: Google rolled out the ability to view impressions by asset (ad copy snippet) and by combination (complete ad units) in the week before the article was published.
facts.quote: Just this past week, Google did roll out the ability to view impressions by asset (ad copy snippet) as well as impressions by combination (complete ad units).
